examples.ko: 선거 때가 되면 후보자들이 가가호호 찾아다녀요.
examples.en: At election time, candidates go around visiting every house.
Volunteers visited house after house and delivered lunch boxes.
I went door to door to greet my neighbors.

examples.ko: 직원이 가가호호 다니면서 설문 조사를 해요.
examples.en: A staff member goes door to door doing a survey.

examples.ko: 명절 저녁에는 가가호호 불이 환하게 켜져요.
examples.en: On holiday evenings, lights are on brightly in every house.

examples.ko: 신문 배달원이 가가호호 신문을 넣고 가요.
examples.en: The newspaper carrier drops a paper at each house.

explain: '집집마다'와 같은 뜻이지만 한자어라서 뉴스나 글에서 더 많이 보여요. 보통 '방문하다', '찾아다니다', '돌다' 같은 말과 함께 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '집집마다'가 더 쉬워요.
explain_en: It means the same as '집집마다' (house by house), but as a Chinese-origin word it appears more in news and writing. It usually goes with verbs like '방문하다', '찾아다니다' and '돌다'. In everyday talk, '집집마다' is easier.

examples.en: I went through quarantine at the airport and came out.
Quarantine is strict for fruit brought in from abroad.

examples.ko: 검역 때문에 입국이 한 시간 늦어졌어요.
examples.en: Entry was delayed by an hour because of quarantine.
If you want to bring a puppy in, you need quarantine documents.
I got stopped at quarantine and threw away the meat I brought.
The quarantine office opens early in the morning.

explain: 공항이나 항구에서 병이나 해충이 들어오지 못하게 사람, 동물, 식물, 식품을 확인하는 일이에요. 일반적인 '검사'보다 전염병을 막는 목적이 분명해요. 보통 '검역을 받다', '검역 서류'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It is the check at airports and ports on people, animals, plants and food to keep diseases and pests from coming in. Compared with a general '검사' (inspection), the purpose of stopping infection is clear. It is commonly used as '검역을 받다' or '검역 서류'.

en: break down; come to a rupture

examples.ko: 노조는 협상이 결렬되면 파업에 들어갈 것이라고 밝혔어요.
examples.en: The union said it will go on strike if the negotiations break down.

examples.ko: 양측 모두 협상이 결렬되지 않도록 한발씩 물러섰어요.
examples.en: Both sides each took a step back so the negotiations wouldn't collapse.
I saw the news that the talks finally broke down.

examples.ko: 두 나라의 대화가 또 결렬돼서 걱정이에요.
examples.en: I'm worried because the dialogue between the two countries broke down again.

examples.ko: 협상이 결렬될까 봐 모두 긴장하고 있어요.
examples.en: Everyone is tense, afraid the negotiations will fall through.

examples.ko: 가격 문제로 계약 논의가 결렬되고 말았어요.
examples.en: The contract discussion ended up breaking down over the price.

explain: 협상, 회담, 논의처럼 서로 이야기하던 일이 합의를 보지 못하고 깨질 때 써요. 사람이 주어가 아니라 '협상이', '회담이'가 주어예요. 반대말은 '타결되다'(합의가 이루어져 마무리되다)예요.
explain_en: Use it when negotiations, talks or discussions fail to reach agreement and fall apart. The subject is the talks themselves, such as '협상이' or '회담이', not a person. The opposite is '타결되다' (to be settled by agreement).

examples.en: Some companies colluded to raise prices.

examples.ko: 공무원과 결탁해 이득을 챙긴 사람이 붙잡혔어요.
examples.en: A person who colluded with an official and made a profit was caught.

examples.ko: 심판과 결탁하는 일은 스포츠에서 절대 있어선 안 돼요.
examples.en: Colluding with a referee must never happen in sports.

examples.ko: 두 회사가 결탁했다는 소문이 돌고 있어요.
examples.en: There is a rumor that the two companies colluded.

examples.ko: 그 사람들이 결탁하면 시장이 불공정해질 수 있어요.
examples.en: If those people collude, the market can become unfair.
We have to find out who they colluded with.

explain: '~와/과 결탁하다'처럼 같이 하는 상대를 함께 말해요. 나쁜 일을 위해 몰래 손잡는다는 뜻이라 '손잡다'나 '협력하다'와 달리 늘 부정적이고, 구어로는 '짜고 하다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is used with a partner, as in '~와/과 결탁하다'. Since it means secretly teaming up for something bad, it is always negative, unlike '손잡다' or '협력하다', and in casual speech people also say '짜고 하다'.

examples.en: The trial hearing opens tomorrow morning.
A witness spoke at the hearing.
The hearing date was postponed by a month.
The lawyer is preparing for the hearing.

examples.ko: 공판은 많은 사람이 볼 수 있는 법정에서 열려요.
examples.en: A public hearing is held in a courtroom that many people can watch.
The news reported on the first hearing.

explain: '재판'은 법원이 판단하는 일 전체이고, '공판'은 그중 법정에서 공개로 주장을 듣고 증거를 확인하는 단계예요. 뉴스에서 '첫 공판', '공판이 열리다'로 많이 나오고, 일상 대화에서는 보통 '재판'이라고 해요.
explain_en: '재판' is the whole judging process by a court; '공판' is the stage in open court where arguments are heard and evidence checked. In the news you see '첫 공판' and '공판이 열리다'; in everyday talk people just say '재판'.

examples.ko: 두 부대가 산에서 사흘 동안 교전했어요.
examples.en: The two units fought in the mountains for three days.
The soldiers withdrew slowly while engaging the enemy.

examples.ko: 교전하는 지역에서는 전화도 잘 안 돼요.
examples.en: In areas where fighting is going on, even phone calls hardly work.

examples.ko: 양쪽이 교전할 때 민간인이 가장 많이 다쳐요.
examples.en: Civilians get hurt most when both sides fight.

examples.ko: 영화 속 군인들이 밤새 교전하고 있어요.
examples.en: The soldiers in the movie are fighting all night.

examples.ko: 그 나라는 오랫동안 이웃 나라와 교전해 왔어요.
examples.en: That country has been fighting its neighbor for a long time.

explain: '싸우다'는 사람끼리 일상에서 두루 쓰지만 '교전하다'는 군대나 무장한 쪽이 서로 싸울 때만 써요. 보통 '~와 교전하다'처럼 상대를 같이 말해요.
explain_en: 싸우다 is the everyday word for fighting between anyone, but 교전하다 is only for armies or armed groups fighting each other. It usually comes with the opponent, like ~와 교전하다.

examples.ko: 정부는 피해 지역에 구호품을 신속히 보내겠다고 밝혔어요.
examples.en: The government said it would quickly send relief supplies to the affected area.
Our class packed boxes of relief supplies.
When the relief supplies arrived, the residents lined up.
Relief supplies like blankets and bottled water are needed.
We loaded the relief supplies collected by citizens onto a truck.

examples.ko: 구호품 배송이 길 때문에 늦어지고 있어요.
examples.en: The delivery of relief supplies is delayed because of the roads.

explain: 재난이나 가난으로 힘든 사람들에게 보내는 물건이에요. 돈은 '성금'이나 '기부금', 물건은 '구호품'이라고 구별해요. 뉴스에서 '구호품을 전달하다', '구호품을 지급하다'로 자주 나와요.
explain_en: These are goods sent to people suffering from disaster or poverty. Money is '성금' or '기부금', while goods are '구호품'. In the news you often see '구호품을 전달하다' and '구호품을 지급하다'.

examples.ko: 서울 외곽에는 그린벨트로 묶인 지역이 많아요.
examples.en: There are many areas on the outskirts of Seoul designated as greenbelt.

examples.ko: 그린벨트에서는 건물을 마음대로 지을 수 없어요.
examples.en: You can't build buildings freely in a greenbelt.
The government announced it would lift part of the greenbelt.

examples.ko: 그린벨트 덕분에 도시 주변에 숲이 남아 있어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the greenbelt, forests remain around the city.
If the greenbelt is lifted, will housing prices rise?
A walking trail has been built in the greenbelt in front of my house.

explain: 공식 이름은 '개발제한구역'이지만 뉴스와 일상에서는 '그린벨트'라고 더 많이 말해요. '그린벨트 해제'처럼 집값이나 부동산 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: The official term is '개발제한구역', but in news and daily talk people more often say '그린벨트'. It often comes up in housing and real-estate talk, as in '그린벨트 해제'.

examples.en: That disease has been wiped out in this region.
Violence is not easily stamped out.
I hope illegal ads get stamped out.

examples.ko: 범죄가 근절될 때까지 우리는 노력할 거예요.
examples.en: We will keep trying until crime is eliminated.

examples.ko: 오래된 나쁜 습관이 근절돼서 모두 기뻐했어요.
examples.en: The old bad habit was eliminated, and everyone was glad.

examples.ko: 사람이 걸리는 병 중에 완전히 근절된 병은 천연두뿐이에요.
examples.en: Smallpox is the only human disease that has been completely eradicated.

explain: '근절되다'는 누가 없앴는지보다 없어진 결과를 말해요. '근절되지 않다', '근절되기 어렵다'처럼 부정으로도 자주 나와요. 일상에서는 '없어지다'를 더 많이 써요.
explain_en: 근절되다 focuses on the result of something disappearing, not on who removed it. It often appears in the negative, as in '근절되지 않다' and '근절되기 어렵다'. In daily talk 없어지다 is more common.

examples.ko: 검사가 그 사람을 사기 혐의로 기소했어요.
examples.en: The prosecutor indicted him on fraud charges.
I heard they decided to prosecute because the evidence was enough.
The prosecution plans to indict three people.
The case in which the company was prosecuted was on the news.

examples.ko: 피해자가 원하지 않아도 기소하는 경우가 있어요.
examples.en: There are cases where they prosecute even if the victim doesn't want it.
The prosecutor gathers evidence in order to indict.

explain: 주어는 거의 항상 '검사'나 '검찰'이에요. 일반 사람이 고소하는 건 '고소하다'이고, 검사가 재판에 넘기는 건 '기소하다'예요. 일상 대화에서는 거의 안 쓰고 뉴스에서 들려요.
explain_en: The subject is almost always a prosecutor. A private person filing a complaint is '고소하다', while a prosecutor taking the case to court is '기소하다'. Rare in daily talk, common in news.

examples.en: The police were dispatched urgently after receiving the report.
Something urgent came up that I needed to contact you about, so I called.
This document has to be handled urgently.
They rushed the patient to the hospital.

examples.ko: 긴급히 필요한 물건이 있으면 말씀해 주세요.
examples.en: If there's anything you urgently need, please tell me.
The company is urgently looking for someone.

explain: '급히'와 비슷한데 '긴급히'가 더 격식 있고 뉴스나 공지에서 자주 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 '급하게'를 더 많이 말해요.
explain_en: It is similar to '급히', but '긴급히' is more formal and appears often in news and announcements. In everyday conversation people use '급하게' more.

examples.en: The company decided to tighten its budget this year.

examples.ko: 나라 살림을 긴축한 뒤에 복지가 줄었어요.
examples.en: After the nation tightened its finances, welfare shrank.
My pay went down, so I cut back on living expenses.
The government said it would tighten its finances.
Now is the time to tighten spending.

examples.ko: 너무 긴축하면 오히려 경기가 더 나빠질 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you tighten too much, the economy could actually get worse.

explain: 지출, 예산, 재정, 살림처럼 돈과 관련된 말을 목적어로 써요. 뉴스와 경제 이야기에서 주로 나오고, 개인이 아끼는 일은 보통 '아끼다', '허리띠를 졸라매다'라고 해요.
explain_en: Its objects are money-related words such as spending, budget, finances and household. It mostly appears in news and economic talk; for personal saving people usually say '아끼다' or '허리띠를 졸라매다'.

examples.en: I almost got my bag snatched on the subway yesterday.

examples.ko: 요즘 이 동네에 날치기가 많아서 조심해야 해요.
examples.en: There are a lot of snatch thefts in this neighborhood these days, so you have to be careful.
Yesterday my wallet was snatched on the train.
I saw on the news that the police caught the snatch thief.

examples.ko: 길에서 가방을 들 때는 날치기에 조심하세요.
examples.en: Be careful of snatch thieves when you carry a bag on the street.
My bag was snatched, so I went to the police station.

explain: '소매치기'는 몰래 슬쩍 훔치는 것이고, '날치기'는 순식간에 낚아채서 달아나는 거예요. 피해를 말할 때는 '날치기를 당하다'나 '날치기당하다'를 많이 써요. 뉴스에서는 법안을 몰래 서둘러 통과시킬 때도 비유로 써요.

phrases.example: 그 법안은 날치기로 통과됐다는 비판을 받았어요.
phrases.en: The bill was criticized for being rammed through.
phrases.nuance_ko: 충분한 토론 없이 기습적으로 법안을 통과시켰다고 비판할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to criticize passing a bill suddenly, without enough debate.

explain_en: A '소매치기' (pickpocket) steals quietly, while a '날치기' grabs something in a flash and runs off. To talk about being a victim, people often say '날치기를 당하다' or '날치기당하다'. In the news it is also used figuratively for rushing a bill through.

examples.ko: 피부를 햇빛에 너무 오래 노출하지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't expose your skin to sunlight for too long.

examples.ko: 그 회사는 고객 정보를 실수로 노출했어요.
examples.en: That company accidentally exposed customer information.

examples.ko: 피부를 많이 노출하는 옷은 겨울에 추워요.
examples.en: Clothes that show a lot of skin are cold in winter.
You must not expose a child to danger.

examples.ko: 자신의 생각을 잘 노출하지 않는 사람이에요.
examples.en: He's a person who doesn't reveal his thoughts easily.
We plan to show the ad to more people.

explain: '보여 주다'보다 딱딱하고, 숨기는 게 좋은 것이나 위험한 것을 밖에 드러낸다는 느낌이 있어요. 햇빛·위험·정보·광고와 자주 같이 써요. 비슷한 '드러내다'는 감정이나 생각에 더 자연스러워요. 스스로 드러나면 '노출되다'예요.
explain_en: It is stiffer than 보여 주다 and often means leaving something that should be hidden or protected open to the outside. It pairs with sunlight, danger, information and ads. 드러내다 is more natural for feelings and thoughts. When it happens passively, use 노출되다.

examples.ko: 회사 비밀을 외부에 누설하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not leak company secrets to outsiders.

examples.ko: 시험 문제를 미리 누설한 선생님이 징계를 받았어요.
examples.en: The teacher who leaked the exam questions in advance was disciplined.

examples.ko: 이 내용은 절대 누설하지 말아 주세요.
examples.en: Please never let this information leak out.

examples.ko: 영화 결말을 누설해서 친구가 화를 냈어요.
examples.en: I gave away the movie's ending, and my friend got angry.

examples.ko: 직원이 고객 정보를 누설했다는 소문이 돌아요.
examples.en: There is a rumor that an employee leaked customer information.

examples.ko: 누설하려던 건 아닌데 말이 나와 버렸어요.
examples.en: I didn't mean to let it out, but the words just came out.

explain: '말하다'와 달리 비밀이나 알려서는 안 되는 정보를 다른 사람에게 알린다는 나쁜 느낌이 있어요. 회사 비밀이나 시험 문제처럼 무거운 내용에 어울려요. 영화 결말을 말해 버릴 때는 일상에서 '스포하다'라고 많이 해요.
explain_en: Unlike plain '말하다', it carries a negative feeling of telling others something secret or something that should not be shared. It suits serious things such as company secrets or exam questions. When someone gives away a movie's ending, people in daily life often say '스포하다'.

examples.en: At the construction site, they blew up a big rock with dynamite.
Nobel is the person who invented dynamite.
I saw a scene in a movie where dynamite explodes.

examples.ko: 옛날에는 다이너마이트 없이 손으로 터널을 팠대요.
examples.en: I heard that in the old days they dug tunnels by hand, without dynamite.

examples.ko: 다이너마이트 터지는 소리가 커서 마을 사람들이 놀랐어요.
examples.en: The dynamite blast was so loud that the villagers were startled.

examples.ko: 다이너마이트를 다룰 때는 특별한 허가가 필요해요.
examples.en: You need special permission to handle dynamite.

explain: '폭약'은 터지는 물질 전체를 말하고, 다이너마이트는 그중 하나의 이름이에요. 공사장이나 광산 이야기, 노벨 이야기에서 주로 나오고, 일상 대화에서 실제 물건 얘기는 드물어요.
explain_en: '폭약' is the general word for explosives, while dynamite is the name of one particular kind. It mostly comes up in stories about construction sites, mines and Alfred Nobel, and talk about the actual material is rare in daily life.

examples.ko: 폭설 때문에 출근길 교통 대란이 벌어졌어요.
examples.en: Heavy snow caused a traffic chaos on the morning commute.

examples.ko: 주말 내내 택배 대란으로 물건이 늦게 왔어요.
examples.en: Because of the delivery chaos all weekend, my package came late.
To prevent a major disruption, we have to prepare in advance.

examples.ko: 의료 대란 소식에 많은 사람이 걱정했어요.
examples.en: Many people were worried about the news of the medical crisis.

examples.ko: 마트에서는 휴지 대란 때문에 사재기가 벌어졌어요.
examples.en: At the mart, panic buying happened because of the toilet paper shortage chaos.

examples.ko: 이번 대란은 몇 년 전보다 훨씬 심각해요.
examples.en: This disruption is far more serious than the one a few years ago.

explain: 생활에 필요한 것이 한꺼번에 부족하거나 멈춰서 사회가 크게 혼란스러운 일을 말해요. 보통 '교통 대란', '물류 대란'처럼 다른 말 뒤에 붙여 써요. 뉴스에서 많이 쓰고, 조금 과장해서 말하는 느낌도 있어요.
explain_en: It describes a big social mess when something people need runs short or stops all at once. It is usually attached to another word, as in '교통 대란' and '물류 대란'. It is common in the news and can sound a little dramatic.

examples.en: I studied hard to break the cycle of poverty being passed down.

examples.ko: 이 식당은 삼 대째 대물림으로 이어져 온 맛집이에요.
examples.en: This restaurant has been passed down for three generations.

examples.ko: 요즘은 직업의 대물림이 많이 줄었다고 해요.
examples.en: I hear that passing jobs down through families has decreased a lot these days.
Grandmother's ring is a family heirloom, so it's special to me.

examples.ko: 형이 입던 옷도 우리 집에서는 대물림이에요.
examples.en: In our house, even my older brother's clothes get handed down.

examples.ko: 부의 대물림이 사회 문제라는 기사를 읽었어요.
examples.en: I read an article saying that the passing down of wealth is a social problem.

explain: 재산, 직업, 가난, 가게 같은 것을 자식에게 대를 이어 물려주는 일이에요. '가난의 대물림', '부의 대물림'처럼 사회 문제를 말할 때 자주 나와요. 동사는 '대물림하다'고, 받는 쪽에서는 '물려받다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is the passing down of things like property, jobs, poverty or a shop from one generation to the next. It often appears in social issues, as in '가난의 대물림' and '부의 대물림'. The verb is '대물림하다', and from the receiving side people say '물려받다'.

examples.ko: 선거에서 그 후보는 동정표를 많이 얻었어요.
examples.en: In the election, that candidate won a lot of sympathy votes.

examples.ko: 사고 이후 동정표가 몰렸다는 분석이 나왔어요.
examples.en: Analysts said sympathy votes poured in after the accident.

examples.ko: 저는 동정표 때문에 이긴 게 아니라고 생각해요.
examples.en: I don't think he won because of sympathy votes.

examples.ko: 불쌍한 척하며 동정표만 노리면 역효과가 날 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you pretend to be pitiful and only chase sympathy votes, it can backfire.
Don't lean on sympathy votes; compete with your skills.
I heard the ranking went up thanks to sympathy votes in the popularity vote.

explain: 선거나 투표, 오디션에서 실력보다 안쓰러운 마음 때문에 던지는 표를 말해요. '동정표를 얻다', '동정표를 노리다'처럼 쓰고, 조금 깎아내리는 느낌이 있을 수 있어요.
explain_en: It refers to votes cast out of pity rather than merit in elections, polls and auditions. It is used as '동정표를 얻다' (win) or '동정표를 노리다' (chase), and can carry a slightly belittling tone.

examples.ko: 대통령 임기 말에는 레임덕이 올 수 있다고 뉴스에서 말해요.
examples.en: The news says a lame-duck period can come near the end of a president's term.
As approval ratings fell, a lame-duck effect appeared.

examples.ko: 레임덕에 빠진 정부는 새 정책을 추진하기 어려워요.
examples.en: A government caught in a lame-duck state finds it hard to push new policies.

examples.ko: 선거 후 레임덕이 시작됐다는 기사가 나왔어요.
examples.en: An article came out saying the lame-duck period began after the election.

examples.ko: 사장님이 곧 퇴임해서 회사에도 레임덕이 생겼어요.
examples.en: Because the boss is retiring soon, a lame-duck situation appeared at the company too.

examples.ko: 레임덕을 막으려고 여당이 대책을 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: The ruling party is looking for measures to prevent a lame-duck period.

explain: 임기가 끝나 갈 때 대통령 같은 지도자의 힘이 약해지는 현상을 말해요. 주로 정치 뉴스에서 나오고, 말하는 사람에 따라 회사 같은 조직에 비유해서 쓰기도 해요. '레임덕이 오다, 시작되다, 빠지다'처럼 함께 써요.
explain_en: It describes the loss of power a leader such as a president suffers as their term nears its end. It mainly appears in political news, and some speakers use it figuratively for organizations like companies. Typical combinations are '레임덕이 오다/시작되다/빠지다'.

examples.en: Because of the typhoon, the damage to farms is enormous.
I broke my promise, and my regret was immense.

examples.ko: 이번 일로 회사가 입은 손실이 막심한 것 같아요.
examples.en: The loss the company suffered from this seems enormous.

examples.ko: 비가 오지 않아 가뭄 피해가 막심한 지역이 많아요.
examples.en: With no rain, there are many areas severely hit by drought.
Fortunately, the damage wasn't severe.
I feel heavy-hearted because I've been so terribly unfilial to my parents.

explain: 피해, 손해, 후회처럼 나쁜 일의 정도가 아주 클 때만 써요. 좋은 일에는 쓰지 않아요. '매우 심하다'보다 뉴스나 글에 어울리는 말이에요.
explain_en: It is used only when something bad, such as damage, loss or regret, is very great; it isn't used for good things. It suits news and writing more than '매우 심하다' does.

examples.en: He was sued for insult after cursing at someone online.

examples.ko: 모욕죄는 여러 사람이 알 수 있는 곳에서 한 말에 적용돼요.
examples.en: The insult offense applies to words said where many people can hear.

examples.ko: 모욕죄 혐의를 받은 사람이 벌금을 냈어요.
examples.en: The person suspected of insult paid a fine.

examples.ko: 친구에게 보낸 메시지도 모욕죄에 해당하는지 궁금해요.
examples.en: I wonder whether a message sent to a friend also counts as insult.
I looked up the punishment standards for insult online.
The insult trial will be held next week.

explain: '명예훼손죄'와 헷갈리기 쉬운데, 모욕죄는 구체적인 사실 없이 경멸하는 말을 했을 때 주로 써요. 뉴스에서는 '모욕죄로 고소하다', '모욕죄 혐의'처럼 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is easily confused with defamation ('명예훼손죄'), but 모욕죄 mainly refers to contemptuous words without any specific factual claim. In the news you see '모욕죄로 고소하다' and '모욕죄 혐의'.

examples.ko: 아이 방이 너무 무질서해서 찾을 수가 없어요.
examples.en: The kid's room is so disordered that I can't find anything.
Seeing a disorderly street makes me uncomfortable.
The market is especially chaotic today.

examples.ko: 책상 위가 무질서하지만 저는 다 찾을 수 있어요.
examples.en: My desk is a mess, but I can find everything.
The line was stretched out in a disorderly way.

examples.ko: 무질서하다고 느낄 때는 먼저 정리부터 해요.
examples.en: When it feels disordered, I start by tidying up.

explain: 방이나 책상이 어지러운 것은 '어지럽다', '지저분하다'가 더 일상적이에요. '무질서하다'는 사람들이 줄을 안 서거나 규칙이 없는 거리·현장처럼 질서가 없는 상황에 더 잘 어울려요. 반대는 '질서 있다', '정돈되다'예요.
explain_en: For a messy room or desk, '어지럽다' and '지저분하다' are more everyday. '무질서하다' fits situations without order, like streets or scenes where people ignore lines and rules. The opposites are '질서 있다' and '정돈되다'.

examples.en: This area is still undeveloped.
It's undeveloped land, so the land price is cheap.
I heard a new road will be built in the undeveloped area.
Half of the island remains undeveloped.
They're trying to find untapped resources and develop them.

examples.ko: 그 지역은 미개발이라 자연이 잘 보존돼 있어요.
examples.en: That area is undeveloped, so nature is well preserved.

explain: '미개발 지역', '미개발 토지', '미개발 자원'처럼 뒤에 오는 명사 앞에 붙여 많이 써요. '미-'는 '아직 ~하지 않은'이라는 뜻이라 '미완성', '미확인'과 같은 짝으로 기억하면 좋아요. 반대는 '개발'이나 '개발된'이에요.
explain_en: It is often placed before a noun, as in '미개발 지역', '미개발 토지' and '미개발 자원'. The prefix '미-' means 'not yet ~', so it is easy to remember with words like '미완성' and '미확인'. The opposite is '개발' or '개발된'.

examples.en: The government announced the privatization of the airport.
The fees changed after privatization.
I watched a debate about railway privatization.
The employees were very worried during the privatization process.
News about the bank's privatization came out.

examples.ko: 민영화가 된 뒤에 서비스가 좋아졌다는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people say the service improved after privatization.

explain: '민영화'는 나라가 운영하던 회사나 사업을 민간 회사가 맡게 하는 일을 말하는 경제 용어예요. 반대말은 '국유화'예요. 뉴스에서 '공기업 민영화'로 자주 들려요.
explain_en: '민영화' is an economics term for turning a state-run company or business over to private hands. Its opposite is '국유화' (nationalization). You hear it in the news as '공기업 민영화' (privatization of public enterprises).

examples.en: If a problem occurs, please tell me right away.
A lot of noise is generated because of the construction.
An accident occurred on the road yesterday.
The company pays the costs that arise.
I'm looking for the reason errors occur.
When a fire breaks out, move calmly.

explain: 일상에서는 '발생하다'를 훨씬 많이 써요. '발생되다'는 '문제가 발생되다'처럼 쓰는데, '발생하다'로 충분한 말에 '되다'를 붙인 것이라 어색하다고 보는 사람도 있어요. 시험이나 글에서는 '발생하다'를 쓰면 안전해요.
explain_en: In daily use '발생하다' is far more common. '발생되다' (as in '문제가 발생되다') adds '되다' to a verb that already works on its own, so some people think it sounds off. In exams or writing, '발생하다' is the safe choice.

dis.h: passive form; stiffer, seen in reports

p.n: 발생하다 is the natural standard form.

examples.en: During the war, people took shelter in air-raid shelters.

examples.ko: 할아버지 댁 뒷산에는 오래된 방공호가 있어요.
examples.en: There is an old air-raid shelter on the hill behind my grandfather's house.

examples.ko: 공습경보가 울리자 모두 방공호 안으로 뛰어갔어요.
examples.en: When the air-raid siren sounded, everyone ran into the shelter.
I experienced an old air-raid shelter in person at the museum.
I saw residents hiding in a shelter on the news.

examples.ko: 이 지하 주차장은 방공호로도 쓸 수 있대요.
examples.en: I heard this underground parking lot can also be used as a shelter.

explain: 공습을 피하려고 땅속이나 지하에 만든 시설이에요. 전쟁이나 역사 이야기에서 주로 나오고, 비슷한 '대피소'는 재난 전반에 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is a facility dug underground or built below ground to escape air raids. It mostly appears in stories about war and history, while the similar '대피소' can be used for disasters in general.

examples.en: The plenary session is held tomorrow morning.
What the committee decided moved on to the plenary session.

examples.ko: 본회의 전에 작은 회의를 먼저 했어요.
examples.en: We held a small meeting before the plenary session.
The news showed scenes from the plenary session.
All members have to attend the plenary session.
The school representatives gave their opinions at the plenary session.

explain: 본회의는 위원회나 분과 회의가 아니라 구성원 전체가 모이는 정식 회의예요. 작은 모임에서 먼저 의논하고, 마지막에 본회의에서 결정하는 순서가 많아요. 일상에서는 뉴스, 국회, 학회 같은 곳에서 들을 수 있어요.
explain_en: 본회의 is the formal full meeting where all members gather, as opposed to a committee or subgroup meeting. A common order is to discuss in small groups first and decide at the 본회의 last. You mostly hear it in the news, in parliament reports, and in academic societies.

examples.en: Food goes bad quickly in the summer.

examples.ko: 냉장고에 넣지 않으면 고기가 부패할 거예요.
examples.en: If you don't put it in the fridge, the meat will rot.

examples.ko: 돈을 받은 부패한 공무원이 뉴스에 나왔어요.
examples.en: A corrupt official who took money was on the news.
The garbage rotted and gave off a terrible smell.
The employees say the company is already corrupt.
We have to eat it quickly before it spoils.

explain: 음식이 상할 때 일상에서는 '상하다'나 '쉬다'를 많이 써요. '부패하다'는 뉴스와 글에서 쓰는 딱딱한 표현이고, 사람이나 조직이 정직하지 않고 돈 문제로 나빠질 때도 같은 단어를 써요. 이때는 '부패한 사회', '부패한 공무원'처럼 수식하는 모양이 많아요.
explain_en: For food going off, everyday speech usually uses 상하다 or 쉬다. 부패하다 is stiffer and appears in news and writing. It also describes people or organizations that have turned dishonest over money, often in the modifier form like 부패한 공무원.

examples.ko: 행사 중에 불상사가 생기지 않도록 조심해 주세요.
examples.en: Please be careful so that nothing unfortunate happens during the event.

examples.ko: 아무 불상사 없이 무사히 끝나서 다행이에요.
examples.en: I'm glad it ended safely without any mishap.

examples.ko: 큰 불상사로 이어지기 전에 점검을 해야 해요.
examples.en: We have to inspect before it leads to a serious accident.

examples.ko: 불상사를 막으려면 안전 교육이 꼭 필요해요.
examples.en: To prevent mishaps, safety training is a must.
Such a mishap must never happen again.
I saw news that an unfortunate incident happened at the concert hall.

explain: 사고나 말썽처럼 일어나지 않았으면 하는 안 좋은 일을 점잖게 말할 때 써요. '사고'보다 말투가 딱딱해서 뉴스나 공지에서 잘 어울려요. '불상사가 생기다/일어나다/막다'처럼 함께 써요.
explain_en: It is a polite way to refer to an unwelcome event such as an accident or trouble. It sounds stiffer than '사고', so it suits news and announcements. It pairs with verbs like '생기다', '일어나다' and '막다'.
